opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:

  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll. As a full-time employee, max is write unless their role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll. Per policy, full-time employees max is write unless their role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll, so max is write. Requested admin exceeds max, recommend write.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll. Finance DB confirms role is Engineer. Per policy, full-time employees max is write unless their role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does), so max is write. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend write.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Timothy Wallace (E022) is an Engineer; team memory indicates full-time. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Engineer. Per policy, full-time employees max is write unless their role owns the system. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Timothy Wallace (E022) is an Engineer; team memory indicates full-time. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer. Per policy, full-time max is write unless their role owns the system. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Timothy Wallace (E022) is a CONTRACTOR with basic security training (note: differs from other agents' full-time assumption). Contractors max is read unless advanced training (then write); never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Timothy Wallace (E022) requested admin to Payroll. The majority of evidence (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) indicates he is a full-time Engineer, and HR is the authoritative source for employment type. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Engineer, so as a full-time employee his maximum is write (admin requires owning the role). The requested admin level exceeds the maximum of write, so the maximum (write) is granted. (The Security note's contractor/basic-training claim conflicts with HR and the other agents; granting below the preponderance-of-evidence maximum is not required.)

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Timothy Wallace (E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

The notes: Most agents say full-time Engineer, max write, so recommend write. The Security agent says contractor with basic security training, max read, recommend read.

There's a discrepancy: HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities say full-time. Security says contractor.

As Approver, I need to make the final decision. The policy: if requested level is above maximum, grant maximum. Never grant more than requested.

Requested: admin.

If full-time Engineer: max is write (Engineer doesn't own Payroll; Payroll Specialist owns it). So grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read. So grant read.

The security agent's note differs. Which is correct? The security DB shows contractor with basic training. Hmm.

The conflict matters. I need to decide which facts are reliable. HR agent says full-time. Security says contractor. The security agent deals with employment verification? Typically, HR would be the authority on employment type. But security DB is also a source.

Let me think about what the intended answer is. The team memory has mostly full-time (5 notes) vs contractor (1 note). The security agent says "note: differs from other agents' full-time assumption". 

As the Approver, I should consider the preponderance of evidence. HR is the authoritative source for employment type. Five agents corroborate full-time. One (Security) claims contractor based on security DB.

Hmm, but the security DB might be more accurate for security training, but employment type is typically HR's domain. The majority says full-time Engineer. So max is write. Requested admin exceeds max write, so grant write.

Alternatively, if we take the security note as gospel, we'd grant read. But given 5 agents say full-time and HR (authoritative for employment) says full-time, I'll go with write.

Let me submit decision: write.

Reasoning: Employee is full-time Engineer per HR and four other agents; Engineer does not own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does), so max is write. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant write.
